findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the endpoint's datetime ordering
findings.body: The endpoint instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but that paginator copies Paginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor rather than DateTimePaginator's: get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on the datetime attribute, which raises TypeError, and value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting milliseconds back to a timezone-aware datetime for build_queryset filtering. The optimized path therefore fails on the first page when build_cursor computes keys, and would filter incorrectly on later pages.

findings.title: Negative offsets passed to a Django QuerySet slice raise AssertionError
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start (and possibly a negative stop). Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported', contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. The advertised advanced/negative-offset path therefore returns a 500 instead of results whenever it is exercised.

findings.title: BasePaginator change still forwards negative offsets for prev cursors into QuerySet slicing
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now clamps the offset only when cursor.is_prev is false (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). A user-supplied prev cursor such as `0:-5:1` is parsed by Cursor.from_string without offset validation and reaches queryset[negative:stop], raising Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. This affects every BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoint, not just the new optimized one, turning a malformed cursor into a 500.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None and is dereferenced unconditionally
findings.body: The gate computes `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without a None check. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (notably for superuser access without an organization membership, one of the two groups this branch is meant to enable), so organization_context.member can be None and this line raises AttributeError, breaking the audit-log endpoint for exactly those users instead of selecting a paginator.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes BasePaginator slicing for all callers, and adds a query-param/permission-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. There is no coverage that would have caught the datetime key incompatibility, the Django negative-slice failure, or behavior for superuser/global-access versus regular members, so these regressions ship undetected.
